references.text: Moses married Zipporah, the daughter of Jethro (Reuel), establishing the father-in-law relationship mentioned in this verse.
Jethro is identified as a priest in Midian and Moses' father-in-law, the same person who comes to Moses in Exodus 18:6.
Moses took his wife and sons with him to Egypt, the same family members that Jethro now brings back to Moses.
The names of Moses' wife Zipporah and his two sons Gershom and Eliezer are mentioned, who are the same people Jethro brings with him.
Hobab, son of Reuel (Jethro), a Midianite and Moses' father-in-law, refers to the same family relationship.
These verses mark the beginning and end points of Moses' stay with his father-in-law Jethro in Midian.
The verses document the sequence from Jethro's arrival (18:6) to his official participation in worship and fellowship with Israel's leaders (18:12).
This is a direct dialogue sequence where Jethro's arrival (18:6) leads to Moses' explanation of his role (18:15).
